questions.text: Is this a new migration with a unique stamp later than the base branch's newest, touching no applied migration? Is every statement re-runnable?
Does any new table or column hold or link to a person? Where is its erasure line (delete, anonymize, or retain with a reason)?
Which project script applies this to each database (test, eval, dev, prod), and what host will it actually hit?
What is the provenance class of every piece of content this saves (user-authored, user's app, user-viewed, agent-fetched)? Did the user see it?
Are resources bound by id and owner, never by a matching name?
What tenant or scope does each read and write resolve to server-side? What happens when it is missing (deny)?
Which abuse cases apply: domainless user, public-mail domain, uninvited same-domain user, group participant, other-org member?
For every combining or destructive operation: where is the inverse, and what state must be stored now to run it later?
How do ACLs combine? Can any step make a reader set grow without a new granting source? Pre-mortem: six months later a stranger saw our data; how?

budgets.measure: authorization matrix test, forbidden cells returning data

rules.title: Applied migration edited, renamed or deleted
rules.why: Databases that already ran it keep the old version; checksums fail or schemas drift.
rules.confirm: static-proof: git diff --name-status shows M/D/R on a migration that exists on the base
rules.fixHint: restore the file; add a new migration

rules.title: Two migrations share a timestamp
rules.why: Order between them is undefined; one can be skipped on databases that already ran the other.
rules.confirm: static-proof: two entries with the same stamp prefix
rules.fixHint: renumber the newer one after rebasing on the base

rules.title: DDL without IF NOT EXISTS (not safe to re-run)
rules.why: A migration that fails halfway fails again on retry.
rules.confirm: repro-script: apply the migration twice on an empty local database; the second run errors
rules.fixHint: IF NOT EXISTS guards; DO blocks for constraints and enum types

rules.title: Destructive database shortcut (accept-data-loss, migrate reset, DROP DATABASE)
rules.why: One wrong env file and it wipes a shared database; it also leaves no migration history.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the command is in a script or config
rules.fixHint: use the project's named migration scripts against the local test database only

rules.title: New table with user_id/email/author_id while the erasure module is untouched
rules.why: Deleting an account leaves rows behind.
rules.confirm: failing-test: seed a user in every person table, run erasure, query by id/email: rows remain

rules.title: Save/ingest of content that came from fetch, a browser or web search, or with no provenance argument
rules.why: Agent-fetched content poisons the user's store and carries injected instructions.
rules.confirm: failing-test: save with provenance=agent_fetched is accepted

rules.title: Owner-scoped resource chosen by display name
rules.why: A name match picks someone else's resource.
rules.confirm: failing-test: foreign-owner resource with the same name is accepted

rules.title: ACL assigned or spread in merge code instead of a lattice join
rules.why: A private fact turns public after a merge.
rules.confirm: failing-test: merge a private fact into a public entity; an outsider can read it

rules.title: Merge/delete/move with no paired inverse and no stored pre-image
rules.why: Undo is impossible or reconstructs the wrong state.
rules.confirm: failing-test: unmerge(merge(G)) != G on a small graph

verify.text: immutability diff (only A), stamp uniqueness after rebase, lint on new files
replay all migrations on an empty local test database and run the schema drift diff (--exit-code)
schema-to-erasure-registry conformance test, then the erasure round-trip test (second user's rows survive)
authorization matrix (actors x resources x actions) and property-based isolation test
provenance sink tests + injection canary not found in the store
merge/unmerge round-trip property and the no-widening invariant over random command sequences
